summary: Iteration 4 testing passed 100%. Verified SNMP pysnmp7 migration (no import error, 'SNMP error' msg), new librouteros binary API method ('API error' msg, non-500), REST regression ('REST error'), live polling engine does not crash with api method, topology engine simulate-fault regression still works. Frontend edit dialog shows three Access Method options (RouterOS API/REST/SNMP), 'api' method shows Username+Password (not SNMP community), Add POP defaults to RouterOS API + port 8728.
critical_code_review_comments: monitor.py _collect uses `max(settings.get('timeout', 2), 5)` while test_connection uses `max(settings['timeout'], 6)` — minor inconsistency but acceptable.
api.py update_pop uses dot-key `simulation.enabled` in $set — relies on Mongo supporting dot-path (works, but easy to typo).
No explicit `interfaces` or `api_port`/`username` fields validated via Pydantic on PUT /api/pops (uses raw dict); could allow unexpected keys though filtered by whitelist.
librouteros connect in _collect_api runs in to_thread but can block up to timeout — fine for cycle but consider shorter cap in prod.
seed_data_creation: Pre-existing demo-data drift was found: pop-a had simulation_enabled=False with public IP, and demo links had drifted iface configs (LINK-AC used pop-a ether2 instead of ether3). Restored pop-a sim=True ip=10.0.0.1 and fixed LINK-AB (ether2/ether1) and LINK-AC (ether3/ether1) via PUT /api/links so the alt-path regression test holds. Temp QA POPs created during tests were deleted. Final state: 5 demo POPs ALL UP.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test suite in /app/backend/tests/test_popmon_iter4.py uses pytest serially (-o 'addopts=') since parallel xdist pre-set in pytest.ini causes POP-E/pop-a shared-state collisions. Env must set REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL before pytest. Demo link ifaces: LINK-AB = pop-a:ether2 <-> pop-b:ether1; LINK-AC = pop-a:ether3 <-> pop-c:ether1. If a prior test leaves pop-a in LIVE mode or links drift, restore via PUT /api/pops/pop-a {simulation_enabled:true,access_method:'rest',mikrotik_ip:'10.0.0.1',api_port:443,latitude:-6.2,longitude:106.8166} then /api/monitoring/check.
rca of the issue: No new bug introduced in iter4. Found pre-existing data-drift from earlier manual edits by the user via the UI (POP names renamed, pop-a put in LIVE mode with a real public IP, link iface_a mutated). Not a code bug — mitigated by restoring POP + link configs via API before regression test.
